project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to finance a garbage truck for the city of Napoleon, North Dakota. The city used to haul its garbage to a different town, but that town is no longer accepting outside refuse in its landfill. This has led to Napoleon hauling their garbage to a larger city instead. Due to smaller capacity of their existing garbage truck, they have to make the trip to the larger city two times a week. This is costing Napoleon additional expenses in contract services and salary. The 2007 Sterling truck is pushing 90,000 miles. The garbage truck body has had many problems. Specifically, these garbage bodies can only compress garbage so many times before the metal gets fatigued. The city of Napoleon would like to purchase a new garbage truck that has more capacity to hold more refuse, therefore cutting down the number of trips from two to one to the larger citys landfill. The Shell Valley lagoon area to be improved has many deficiencies that inadequately treat the wastewater in the system. With the completion of the project, the waste at the Shell Valley lagoon will be relocated to a consolidated wastewater treatment system and the lagoons located over the Shell Valley aquifer, the main drinking water source for the tribe, will be abandoned to protect the water source. In addition, the consolidated system will allow for additional users to be connected, providing safe waste disposal for residents. This project will benefit 8,669 residents.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to finance sewer lagoon improvements for the residents of the Trenton Indian Service Area in Williams County, N.D. which has 453 residents. The current lagoons are hydraulically and organically overloaded due to growth in the area, resulting in the need to discharge the wetland cell several times throughout the year. The project will renovate and expand existing lagoon cells to increase capacity and water treatment capabilities. With the completion of the lagoon improvement project, Trenton Indian Service Area will be able to provide adequate wastewater treatment for existing and future residents.
